{{Quote|The outlines of what happened some 200,000 years ago are known to every schoolchild: The 13 nations that made up the Battalions of Zhell spent centuries clashing with the forces of the Taungs. During one of their skirmishes, a volcanic eruption destroyed the city of Zhell, shattering the Battalions' power.|Eschul Shaywa, "A LONG TIME AGO..."|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
The '''destruction of Zhell''' was a legendary event described in the ancient epic poem ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]''. The poem gave an account of a long [[Zhell–Taung war|war]] fought around [[200,000 BBY]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Notron]] between the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and the [[Battalions of Zhell]], which were formed by nations of the potentially ancestral [[Human/Legends|Human]] culture known as the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]]. The ninth chapter of the ''Dha Werda Verda'' described Taung [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] preparing to face the Zhell in combat on the following [[Standard day/Legends|day]], with the former assembling at the location referred to as the "[[high place]]" that overlooked the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the latter, known as [[Great Zhell]]. Per the ''Dha Werda Verda'', on the morning of the next day, after the Zhell had been briefly frightened by the appearance of the Taungs at the high place, a sudden [[Volcano/Legends|volcanic]] eruption destroyed Great Zhell and created a high plume of [[Color/Legends|black]] ash that filled Notron's [[Atmosphere/Legends|skies]] for two [[Standard year/Legends|years]].

According to the poem, both the Taungs and the Zhell were nearly rendered extinct by the event. The Taungs, who subsequently were claimed to have subjugated the surviving Zhell, named themselves the ''Dha Werda Verda'', or "Warriors of the Shadow," in recognition of the ash making them appear as emerging from shadows, and they eventually celebrated their victory by [[Poet/Legends|composing]] the poem ''Dha Werda Verda''. Nevertheless, the Zhell were claimed to have eventually recovered from their loss and driven the Taungs off Notron. Hundreds of [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] after the events described in the poem had supposedly taken place, academics had difficulties ascertaining the historicity of the destruction of Zhell, although the [[Ice Crypts]] of Notron&mdash;by that point known as Coruscant&mdash;were theorized to indeed contain [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|archaeological]] evidence connected to that event. Meanwhile, by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the ''Dha Werda Verda'' had gone on to become an important element of the culture of [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscant's]] Human-dominated population.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|Assembled they ascended, in taut Taung lines, to the high place where the Reaver had staked his standard before it was cast down into the mire. They gazed out over the gathering places and walking ways of Great Zhell where they scaled peak and cradled valley, the lines of lights ordering the night. They unfurled the Taung banner, reversed, a reckless thing snapping in the dark, awaiting Zhell eyes. And they performed ceremonies of leave-taking, for now they had died to the world and must be remade among the stars.|The ''Dha Werda Verda''|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
[[File:Coruscant-EotE.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The planet Coruscant, originally known as Notron, was believed to have been the origin point of both Humans and Taungs.]]
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="TEA" /> and that of<ref name="SWTORE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> the [[near-Human]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]] were both<ref name="SWTORE" /> generally<ref name="Author's Cut" /> believed to have [[Homeworld/Legends|hailed]] from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], which was originally known as Notron.<ref name="TEA" /> According to the ancient epic poem ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'',<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[200,000 BBY|200,000 years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]<ref name="Date" /> the warlike<ref name="CSWE Taung">{{CSWECite|III|225|Taung}}</ref> Taungs were engaged in a [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]]-long<ref name="Author's Cut" /> legendary<ref name="NEC" /> [[Zhell–Taung war|war]] against the [[Battalions of Zhell]]. The latter had been formed by the thirteen nations of the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]], a cultural group that had possibly been the ancestral Human population.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

A portion of the ninth of the eleven chapters of the ''Dha Werda Verda'' described Taung [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] at one point attending the [[Funeral/Legends|funeral]] of<ref name="EGTW" /> the revered Taung [[General/Legends|general]] known as the [[Doom of Ulmarah]].<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The warriors were expecting that, without the Doom's [[Commanding officer/Legends|leadership]], they were fated to be destroyed on the following [[Standard day/Legends|day]] by the Zhell forces. Nevertheless,<ref name="EGTW" /> the general<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Rexutu the Unconquerable]] was resolved to face the enemy in combat. He assembled the warriors, and they prepared their [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]], after which the Taungs ascended to the location referred to in the poem as the "[[high place]]," which overlooked the Zhell<ref name="EGTW" /> [[Capital/Legends|capital]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[City/Legends|city]] known as [[Great Zhell]]<ref name="EGTW" />&mdash;or simply Zhell<ref name="Author's Cut" />&mdash;and where the standard of<ref name="EGTW" /> the Taung leader [[Olhak the Reaver]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> had previously been staked at. There, the warriors unfurled the Taung banner and performed ceremonies of leave-taking in preparation for their upcoming inevitable [[Death/Legends|demise]] in battle.<ref name="EGTW" />

==The battle==
{{Quote|But then came a shaking of the ground, and the sun's wan light was eclipsed by a bright and terrible fire that exploded from the rock. The patterns of Great Zhell shivered and broke. And after this came darkness, as the very air turned to black ash. The Zhell fell on their faces in terror, and from the high place we ran in haste to meet them, and we were cloaked in shadow.|The ''Dha Werda Verda''|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
[[File:TaungMartialArtsMaster-GAW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|According to the epic poem ''Dha Werda Verda'', the destruction of the Zhell capital was a turning point in their war against the Taungs (a Taung pictured).]]
The ninth chapter of the ''Dha Werda Verda'' then went on to describe how, upon the dawn of the next day, the Zhell were briefly frightened at the appearance of the Taungs at the high place, with the distance and the glint of the latter's [[Helmet/Legends|helms]] and weapons in the [[Coruscant Prime/Legends|sunlight]] giving rise to a mirage of "phantom warriors." Upon realizing, however, the extent of the outnumbered Taung force, the Zhell<ref name="EGTW" /> [[Army/Legends|army]]<ref name="CatCW" /> proceeded to prepare at a measured pace to march toward the enemy and fight them.<ref name="EGTW" />

At that point, according to the ''Dha Werda Verda'', a bright [[Volcano/Legends|volcanic]] eruption, obscuring the [[Star/Legends|sun]], destroyed Great Zhell. Subsequently,<ref name="EGTW" /> a towering plume of [[Color/Legends|black]] ash<ref name="NEC" /> rose [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] into the [[Atmosphere/Legends|sky]],<ref name="SotE OST">[[Shadows of the Empire (soundtrack)|''Shadows of the Empire'' soundtrack]] {{Ln}}</ref> blotting out the sun<ref name="Author's Cut" /> and casting the land into darkness.<ref name="EGTW" /> Per the poem, the Taungs,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> awestruck by the majesty of the sight,<ref name="Codex">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 03: The Battalions of Zhell}}</ref> observed the ash raining down toward them,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> and the combination of the [[Fire/Legends|fire]] and<ref name="CatCW" /> the destructive ash went on to bury the Zhell forces.<ref name="CSWE Taung" /> The Taungs gathered at the high place, cloaked in the shadow cast by the ash, then charged at their enemy,<ref name="EGTW" /> with the surviving Zhell who saw the Taungs emerging from the darkened skies describing them as "warriors coming from the shadows."<ref name="CSWE Warriors" /> The ''Dha Werda Verda'' poetically described<ref name="EGTW" /> the destruction of Zhell<ref name="Author's Cut" /> as "the Maker" having arrived to "unmake"<ref name="EGTW" /> the world.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Aftermath==
===Legendary societies transformed===
{{Quote|The assembled Taungs watched in awe as ash blotted out the sun and rained down upon them. Taking their opponents' destruction as a sign of divine favor, the Taungs christened themselves Dha Werda Verda, the Shadow Warriors, and celebrated their victory in the epic poem of the same name.|Eschul Shaywa, "A LONG TIME AGO..."|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
Per ''Dha Werda Verda'',<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the Taungs went on to subjugate the Zhell<ref name="Codex" /> nations, the power of which was shattered by the loss of Great Zhell.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The effects of the volcanic eruption nearly eradicated both the Zhell and the Taungs,<ref name="TEA" /> with the ash filling Notron's skies for two [[Standard year/Legends|years]]<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> and casting an immense shadow over the land.<ref name="CSWE Taung" /> The Taungs saw the phenomenon as a sign of [[Mandalorian religion|divine favor]]<ref name="EGTW" /> and a symbol of their destiny<ref name="CSWE Taung" /> and named themselves "Dha Werda Verda,"<ref name="EGTW" /> which translated as "Warriors of the Shadow"<ref name="CSWE Taung" /> or alternately as "Shadow Warriors,"<ref name="EGTW" /> "Dark Warriors,"<ref name="CSWE Taung" /> or "Dark Shadow Warriors."<ref name="SotE OST" /> To celebrate their victory, at some point the Taungs also [[Poet/Legends|composed]] the poem ''Dha Werda Verda'', which gave an account of the destruction of Great Zhell.<ref name="EGTW" />

[[File:Coruscant_view_EII_2.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Coruscant, the supposed former site of Great Zhell prior to its destruction, eventually became a city-covered world.]]
The Zhell were claimed to have recovered from their loss<ref name="Author's Cut" /> and, after years of struggle,<ref name="Codex" /> supposedly drove the Taungs off Notron.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The planet, which eventually came to be known as Coruscant, over [[Time/Legends|time]] became a [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|city-world]] entirely covered in kilometer-deep levels of urban terrain.<ref name="TEA" /> At some point, the [[Ice Crypts]], a network of [[Temperature/Legends|frozen]] [[Cave/Legends|caves]] located near the planet's south pole and containing thirteen [[Mummy/Legends|mummified]] bodies, were discovered. Since many of the bodies were wearing complete body armor, [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|xenoarchaeologists]] theorized that they belonged to the war chieftain leaders of the thirteen Zhell nations, who had retreated into the caves after their defeat by the Taungs and [[Burial/Legends|buried]] themselves alive.<ref name="CSWE IceCrypts">{{CSWECite|II|75|Ice Crypts}}</ref>

Two hundred [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] after the supposed events depicted in the ''Dha Werda Verda'', academics struggled with confirming their historicity. There was no agreement about the site of Great Zhell,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> and [[Geologist/Legends|geologists']] estimates that Coruscant had not experienced volcanic activity for a very long time<ref name="CatCW" /> rendered dating the poem's events problematic, as well. Furthermore, some [[Scholar/Legends|scholars]] even speculated that the conflict between the Zhell and the Taungs had no historic basis whatsoever. In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], the problems with ascertaining the historicity of the destruction of Zhell were mentioned in the ''[[Imperial Center Today]]''{{'s}} contributor [[Eschul Shaywa]]'s article "[[A LONG TIME AGO...]]," which focused on the paucity of historical information regarding the Zhell and the Taungs.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The supposed event was nevertheless noted in a [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]] [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] history [[The Essential Chronology|chronicle]] by the [[Historical Council]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> as well as its [[36 ABY]] [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|updated edition]] by the Council's incarnation under the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]].<ref name="NEC" />

===Impact across the ages===
{{Quote|The Taungs were not human. If the account of the destruction of Zhell is even vaguely accurate, it was a monumental disaster for humanity. So what you have is the descendents of those who survived a near-extinction reciting the poem their oppressors composed to celebrate the event.|Mesh Burzon, "A LONG TIME AGO..."|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
{{GameLS|Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne}}
In [[3628 BBY]],<ref name="JediUnderSiegeDate">{{TOR_updates|5.10.0}}</ref> the [[Krex]] [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] general [[Ardinondu Dipolus Daeruun]] recited<ref name="Jedi Under Siege">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Jedi Under Siege|Ossus}}</ref> the section of the ''Dha Werda Verda'' describing the immediate prelude of the battle<ref name="EGTW" /> when talking to the [[Alliance Commander|Commander]] of the [[Eternal Alliance]] about the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire's]] recently foiled [[Invasion of Ossus|invasion]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]]-led [[Jedi Colony|colony]] on the planet [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]].<ref name="Jedi Under Siege" />
{{Endgame}}

[[File:70RepublicYouthSpeechFinal.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A ceremony held in 21 BBY was one of many occasions on which the inhabitants of Coruscant recited the passage of the ''Dha Werda Verda'' describing the destruction of Zhell.]]
At some point by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="RHNN">{{InsiderCite|70|Republic HoloNet News Core Edition 14:9:04}}</ref> the ''Dha Werda Verda'', particularly the section of the work<ref name="Author's Cut" /> describing the volcanic eruption,<ref name="EGTW" /> had emerged as a mainstay of the culture of the [[Coruscanti/Legends|residents]] of Coruscant<ref name="Author's Cut" />&mdash;the capital world of the Republic<ref name="TEA" />&mdash;being recited in the composition's original [[Notron Cant]] [[Language/Legends|language]] by [[Youngling/Legends|children]] and youths<ref name="Author's Cut" /> and [[Artist/Legends|performers]] at professional stage venues alike.<ref name="Sisar">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref> One such instance was in<ref name="RHNN" /> [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="21 BBY">{{InsiderCite|70|Republic HoloNet News Core Edition 14:9:04}} is set on the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] "14:9:04," which corresponds to [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> when teen members of the [[SAGroup (COMPOR)/Legends|SAGroup]] youth chapter of the [[Commission for the Protection of the Republic/Legends|Commission for the Protection of the Republic]] [[Music/Legends|sang]] the relevant passage of the ''Dha Werda Verda'' during a ceremony held at the [[North Garden]] of Coruscant's [[Monument Plaza/Legends|Monument Plaza]].<ref name="RHNN" /> The [[University of Byblos/Legends|University of Byblos]] [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Mesh Burzon]], however, found it odd that the inhabitants of Coruscant,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> who were primarily Humans,<ref name="TEA" /> venerated a poem composed by the non-Human conquerors of the humanity's ancestors to celebrate an event that nearly resulted in the latter's extinction.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Additionally, enthusiast stage recreations of the battle frequently used replicas of weaponry, such as [[Sword/Legends|swords]] and [[Axe/Legends|great axes]], that had been uncovered at Taung burial sites on<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] planet<ref name="EGtPM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> [[Roon/Legends|Roon]], which Taungs had at one point [[Colonist/Legends|settled]]. Military history scholar [[Hu Jibwe]] found such choice of props anachronistic, viewing it as more likely that such relatively highly developed cultures as the Zhell or the Taungs&mdash;of which the latter would have to have been capable of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel&mdash;would have instead used in combat aircraft and [[Nuclear weapon/Legends|nuclear weapons]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|As published, ''Warfare'' offers a translation of the best-known section of ''Dha Werda Verda'', an epic about the ancient battle between the Zhell and the Taungs.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Shadowsmusic.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The final battle between the Taungs and the Zhell was introduced in the liner notes for the ''Shadows of the Empire'' soundtrack.]]
The final battle between the Taungs and the Zhell was first mentioned in the liner notes for [[Joel McNeely]]'s [[1996]] [[Shadows of the Empire (soundtrack)|''Shadows of the Empire'']] original soundtrack. The passage mentioning the battle accompanied a choral poem written by [[Ben Burtt]].<ref name="SotE OST" /> The [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', authored by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]], included an illustration by [[Bruno Werneck]] that depicted the scene from the ''Dha Werda Verda'' wherein Notron's sun shines upon the Taung warriors assembled at the high place immediately prior to the destruction of Zhell.<ref name="EGTW" /> Furthermore, a section was originally meant to be included in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' that would have identified the destruction of Zhell by name; however, the section was cut before the book's release. It was later released in [[2013]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from the book.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
